<!-- fathom:owned — generated by `fathom init --skills`; safe to delete this line to adopt the file as your own -->

The short path from a fresh clone to a wired repository. The full guides
are in fathom's repository:
[docs/early-testers.md](https://github.com/GeoffMillerAZ/fathom/blob/main/docs/early-testers.md)
(install and daemon),
[docs/adoption/claude-code.md](https://github.com/GeoffMillerAZ/fathom/blob/main/docs/adoption/claude-code.md)
and
[docs/adoption/codex.md](https://github.com/GeoffMillerAZ/fathom/blob/main/docs/adoption/codex.md).

## 1. Build (skip if `fathom` is already on your PATH)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/GeoffMillerAZ/fathom.git && cd fathom
# macOS
CGO_ENABLED=1 MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=14.0 go build -o bin/fathom ./cmd/fathom
# Linux (pure Go, no C compiler)
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o bin/fathom ./cmd/fathom
bin/fathom version   # prints the commit it was built from
```

Put the binary on your `PATH`. `fathom init` writes the path of the binary
that ran it into the hooks.

## 2. Start the daemon

Agents and hooks talk to one `fathom serve-http` on `127.0.0.1:7575`. Start
it before `init`, which ingests through it.

**Any OS, in its own terminal:**

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.fathom/db
fathom serve-http --store ~/.fathom/db/fathom.sqlite \
  --idle-exit=0 --ttl=0 --auto-refresh=true
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7575/healthz   # ok
```

A daemon with no supervisor is bounded by default: it exits within 10
seconds of its parent's death, after 20 minutes with no request, or after 8
hours; it does not re-ingest on its own; and it holds a 512 MiB memory
budget. The flags above lift the idle and lifetime bounds and turn re-ingest
on. Add `--exit-with-parent=false` to run it in the background. For a large
repository, start it with `FATHOM_TENANCY_BUDGET=2GiB` in its environment.

**macOS, daily use:** `fathom daemon install` writes a launchd agent
(`~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.fathom.serve-http.plist`, store
`~/.fathom/db/fathom.sqlite`) for the binary that runs it and starts it;
`fathom daemon status` says whether it serves. Run it from a stable copy of
the binary, never `bin/fathom`: a rebuild truncates a running executable.
fathom's own repository installs that copy with `task deploy` (see
docs/early-testers.md). Linux has no systemd unit yet.

Never restart the daemon from an agent's own sandboxed shell. Hand the
operator the command.

## 3. Register the MCP server (once per machine)

**Claude Code:**

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user fathom http://127.0.0.1:7575/rpc/agent
claude mcp get fathom   # Status: Connected
```

`/rpc/agent` serves the eight default tools: `blast_radius`, `find_symbol`,
`obligations`, `read_source`, `review_diff`, `search`, `symbol_context` and
`verify_plan`. `/rpc/extended` (alias `/rpc/companion`) serves 21: those
eight plus navigation, context and freshness tools. `/rpc` is the full
registry of 25 (docs/mcp-tools.md). Surfaces are not a security boundary.
The stanza `init` writes tells the agent to route by question shape: where
a symbol is defined is `find_symbol`, who calls it is `symbol_context`,
what breaks is `blast_radius`, what governs a file is `obligations`, and a
literal string, config value or log line is `search`.

**Codex** reads `AGENTS.md` natively. Register the MCP server in
`~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.fathom]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:7575/rpc/agent"
```

Codex loads hooks only from the user-global `~/.codex/hooks.json`, so
`init` writes none for it. `fathom harness hooks --harness codex` prints the
entries to merge by hand; `fathom prime` prints the session primer
meanwhile.

**Other harnesses** (Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot): `fathom init --harness
<id>` writes the stanza and `.fathom/` and prints that harness's `mcp add`
line. `fathom harness list` shows which harnesses a session has verified.

**Restart the agent session once** after registering. A running session
does not see tools registered after it started.

## 4. Wire the repository: `fathom init`

From the target repository's root:

```sh
fathom init --skills
```

It is idempotent and additive. It:

1. writes `.fathomignore` if absent. Edit it before the first ingest if the
   repository holds secrets or data: every connected MCP client can read
   the index;
2. ingests the repository through the daemon and confirms it indexed;
3. wires the Claude Code hooks into `.claude/settings.json` (20 entries on
   15 events; `fathom harness hooks --harness claude-code` prints them);
4. scaffolds `.fathom/guard.cue`, `concerns.cue`, `modules.cue` and
   `capabilities.cue`, all commented out;
5. writes the fathom stanza into `AGENTS.md` between fathom markers. A root
   `CLAUDE.md` that exists gets one `@AGENTS.md` import; init never creates
   one;
6. installs the ten shipped skills into `.claude/skills/` and links
   `.agents/skills` to that directory;
7. scaffolds `~/.fathom/config.toml` if absent;
8. prints the steps it does not take for you, such as MCP registration.

Exit codes: `0` wired and indexed; `2` wired, but the daemon is unreachable
or the index is empty (re-run once the daemon is up); `1` a real wiring
failure, such as a file fathom does not own at a skill's path, which init
names and leaves alone.

Flags: `--service NAME` (default: the directory's lowercased basename),
`--url URL` (default `http://localhost:7575` or `$FATHOM_HTTP`), `--harness
claude-code|codex|gemini-cli|cursor|copilot|agents|none`,
`--skills=claude|codex|agents|codex-prompts`, `--json`.

On a re-run, a marked region or skill file someone edited by hand is
reported BLOCKED and left as it is. Delete the marked block and re-run to
take fathom's version. `fathom fleet undo --last` reverses the last apply.

## 5. Optional pieces

- **Rules at the edit.** The edit hook injects nothing until the
  `obligations` layer is compiled once: `fathom compile --service <svc>
  --dry-run=false`. That spends tokens with a configured LLM provider
  (`fathom config --explain`, `fathom providers`). The default provider,
  `none`, makes no model call.
- **A pre-push gate.** Add `fathom verify --service <svc> --plan
  docs/plans/<plan>.md --quiet` to your own pre-push hook. See the
  `fathom-verify` skill.
- **Guards, concerns, capabilities and layer packs:** the `fathom-activate`
  and `fathom-custodian` skills. **Imported review findings:** the
  `fathom-findings` skill. **Cloud sessions:**
  docs/adoption/cloud-sessions.md.

## 6. Done when

```sh
fathom version                         # the commit you built
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7575/healthz  # ok
claude mcp get fathom                  # Connected, after a session restart
fathom doctor
```

- [ ] `find_symbol` on a symbol you know returns a hit with `"tier":
      "verified"`.
- [ ] `fathom verify --service <svc> --plan docs/plans/<file>.md` exits `0`
      on a clean plan.
- [ ] `fathom doctor` has no FAIL row you cannot explain. In v0.11.0 three
      rows can fail on a correct fresh install: `lefthook_gates` (the
      repository has no `lefthook.yml`), `obligations_served` (the layer is
      not compiled yet) and `surface_traffic` (no tool call yet). The
      `fathom-doctor` skill reads the rest.
- [ ] The first session line may report `wiring drift: N stale binary
      path(s)` right after `init`, because init wrote an absolute binary
      path. When `fathom doctor` shows `wiring_drift` PASS, that line is a
      false signal.
- [ ] Anything that misbehaves is filed with the `fathom-feedback` skill.
